newsitem.title: USA: Maine opponents of same-sex marriages force vote.
newsitem.headline: Maine opponents of same-sex marriages force vote.

text.p: Supporters of a ban on same-sex marriages in Maine have collected enough signatures to force a referendum vote on the issue, the Secretary of State's office ruled Friday.

The ruling means Maine voters will consider the proposal during the Nov. 4, 1997, election unless it is enacted into law earlier by the Legislature and Gov. Angus King. Polls have indicated the referendum would pass.

Opponents of the ban have said that because they believe the courts will strike down the measure as unconstitutional regardless of the way it may become law, they may ask the Legislature to enact it directly and spare the state from a divisive campaign.
The measure proposed by Concerned Maine Families would prohibit Maine from officially recognising marriages between two people of the same sex even if the marriage is recognised in another state.
The Portland-based group collected 62,032 valid signatures, nearly 11,000 more than needed, according to Secretary of State Dan Gwadosky.
The Legislature is considering gay rights legislation this year.
